flagged_sentences: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas, on November 13, 2026, at about 4:47 p.m. Central — 22:47 UTC.
Catch time: about 21:21 UTC, 3:21 p.m. Central at Starbase, November 14.
It reached orbit, deployed all twenty-six satellites, and completed about fourteen orbits on a mission lasting about 22.5 hours.
Deployment of the twenty-six Starlink V3 satellites begins about thirty-five minutes after liftoff, into an orbit around 275 kilometers.
The payload was twenty-six Starlink V3 satellites, the first operational V3 batch flown on Starship.
It performed a landing burn, cut the engines off while hovering, then the flight termination system activated on splashdown.
SpaceX has described that abort as the system correctly prioritizing pad safety.
Reporting on Flight 15 describes a banking approach, three Raptors for the flip and the slowdown, then one engine near hover.
As of November 15, detailed post-catch inspection results had not been published.

Elon Musk, after the flight, pointed to a booster fuel and performance issue, said it was fixable with engine and software updates, and said it does not change the timeline to high-volume reusable flights.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated SpaceX on the launch and the catch and expressed interest in Starlink capability for Artemis III.
Around 20:23 UTC on November 14, Ship 42 does the deorbit burn.
as of November 15, SpaceX had not released official details on inspections, turnaround, or reflight.
Pre-flight reporting had pointed to a December 2026 target, possibly the first Starship launch from LC-39A in Florida, with likely vehicles Booster 23 and Ship 43.
Gwynne Shotwell, before the flight, had pointed to FAA licensing support for return-to-launch-site and catch operations.
On SPCX, post-flight reporting in the research did not describe a dramatic move tied directly to the Flight 15 outcome.

claims.claim: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Pad 2 at Starbase on November 13, 2026, at about 4:47 p.m. CST (22:47 UTC) on Booster 22 and Ship 42.
claims.episode_span: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas, on November 13, 2026, at about 4:47 p.m. Central — 22:47 UTC.
claims.supporting_quote: Liftoff Nov 13, 2026, ~4:47 p.m. CST (22:47 UTC) from Pad 2/Starbase on Booster 22 + Ship 42.

claims.claim: The Super Heavy booster catch attempt was aborted about T+6:35, and Booster 22 was diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown.
claims.episode_span: About six minutes and thirty-five seconds after liftoff, the booster catch attempt was aborted.
claims.supporting_quote: The booster catch, planned at about T+6:35 , did not happen: SpaceX diverted Super Heavy to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf.

claims.claim: Ship 42 was caught by the tower arms at about 3:21 p.m. CST (21:21 UTC) on November 14, 2026, the first tower catch of an orbital-class Starship upper stage.
claims.episode_span: Catch time: about 21:21 UTC, 3:21 p.m. Central at Starbase, November 14.
claims.supporting_quote: the first orbital-class upper-stage tower catch

claims.claim: Ship 42 completed about 14 orbits on a mission lasting about 22.5 hours.
claims.episode_span: It reached orbit, deployed all twenty-six satellites, and completed about fourteen orbits on a mission lasting about 22.5 hours.
claims.supporting_quote: Ship reached orbit, deployed payload, completed ~14 orbits/~22.5-hour mission

claims.claim: All 26 Starlink V3 satellites were successfully deployed into an orbit around 275 km starting about T+35 minutes, and they were confirmed in contact and raising orbits.
claims.episode_span: Deployment of the twenty-six Starlink V3 satellites begins about thirty-five minutes after liftoff, into an orbit around 275 kilometers.
claims.supporting_quote: All 26 satellites successfully deployed into orbit (~275 km) starting ~T+35 min; contact confirmed and they are raising orbits.

claims.claim: The Flight 15 payload was the first operational Starlink V3 batch flown on Starship.
claims.episode_span: The payload was twenty-six Starlink V3 satellites, the first operational V3 batch flown on Starship.
claims.supporting_quote: First operational Starlink V3 batch flown on Starship.

claims.claim: Booster 22's boostback burn ended early due to a low fuel-mass alarm, and its GNC system aborted the catch as unsafe.
claims.episode_span: Reporting, including SpaceX’s own account as relayed by outlets covering the flight, ties that to a low fuel-mass alarm.
claims.supporting_quote: Early indications are that the booster ended its boostback [burn] early due to a low fuel mass alarm,

claims.claim: After the abort, Booster 22 performed a landing burn, cut engines off while hovering, and the flight termination system activated on splashdown.
claims.episode_span: It performed a landing burn, cut the engines off while hovering, then the flight termination system activated on splashdown.
claims.supporting_quote: Performed landing burn (engines cut off while hovering), then flight termination system (FTS) activated on splashdown.

claims.claim: SpaceX described the booster abort as the system correctly prioritizing pad safety.
claims.episode_span: SpaceX has described that abort as the system correctly prioritizing pad safety.
claims.supporting_quote: SpaceX described it as the system correctly prioritizing pad safety.

claims.claim: Ship 42's heat shield was inspected before reentry by camera-equipped Starlink satellites and reported in good shape for return.
claims.episode_span: Before reentry, the heat shield was inspected from orbit by camera-equipped Starlink satellites and reported in good posture, good shape for return.
claims.supporting_quote: The company confirmed the heat shield was in "good posture for a reentry and return to the launch site."

claims.claim: The Ship catch sequence used a banking approach, three Raptors for the landing flip and slow descent, then reduction to one engine near hover.
claims.episode_span: Reporting on Flight 15 describes a banking approach, three Raptors for the flip and the slowdown, then one engine near hover.
claims.source_title: Why Catching Starship Ship Is Harder
claims.supporting_quote: Reentry/landing burn/catch sequence matched plans (three engines for flip, reduction to one near hover).

claims.claim: SpaceX posted “Mechazilla catches Starship!” after the Ship catch.
claims.episode_span: SpaceX posted “Mechazilla catches Starship!”
claims.supporting_quote: SpaceX posted “Mechazilla catches Starship!” and summarized the flight on its site, highlighting the historic ship catch and full reusability progress.

claims.claim: No detailed post-catch heat-shield or structural inspection results for Ship 42 had been published as of November 15, 2026.
claims.episode_span: As of November 15, detailed post-catch inspection results had not been published.
claims.supporting_quote: No detailed post-catch heat shield or structural inspection results published as of Nov 15.

claims.claim: Elon Musk said the booster fuel and performance issue was fixable via engine and software updates and did not change the timeline to high-volume reusable flights.
claims.episode_span: Elon Musk, after the flight, pointed to a booster fuel and performance issue, said it was fixable with engine and software updates, and said it does not change the timeline to high-volume reusable flights.
claims.source_title: Here’s why the Flight 15 booster catch was abandoned
claims.supporting_quote: Elon Musk noted booster fuel/performance issue (fixable via engine/software updates) but stated it does not change timeline to high-volume reusable flights.

claims.claim: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated SpaceX on the launch and catch and expressed interest in Starlink capability for Artemis III.
claims.episode_span: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated SpaceX on the launch and the catch and expressed interest in Starlink capability for Artemis III.
claims.supporting_quote: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated SpaceX on the launch/catch and expressed interest in Starlink capability for Artemis III.

claims.claim: Ship 42 performed a deorbit burn at about 20:23 UTC on November 14, 2026.
claims.episode_span: Around 20:23 UTC on November 14, Ship 42 does the deorbit burn.
claims.supporting_quote: deorbit burn ~20:23 UTC Nov 14, reentered, flipped with landing burn, and was caught by tower arms

claims.claim: As of November 15, 2026, no official details had been released on Ship 42 inspections, turnaround, or reflight.
claims.episode_span: as of November 15, SpaceX had not released official details on inspections, turnaround, or reflight.
claims.supporting_quote: No official details released as of Nov 15 on inspections, turnaround, or reflight.

claims.claim: No official date or vehicles had been announced for Flight 16 as of November 15, 2026; pre-flight reporting pointed to a December 2026 target, possibly from LC-39A, with likely vehicles Booster 23 and Ship 43.
claims.episode_span: Pre-flight reporting had pointed to a December 2026 target, possibly the first Starship launch from LC-39A in Florida, with likely vehicles Booster 23 and Ship 43.
claims.supporting_quote: No date or vehicles officially announced as of Nov 15, 2026. Pre-flight reporting pointed to a December 2026 target (possibly first Starship launch from LC-39A, Florida) with likely vehicles Booster 23/Ship 43.

claims.claim: Gwynne Shotwell had pre-flight comments on FAA licensing support for return-to-launch-site and catch operations.
claims.episode_span: Gwynne Shotwell, before the flight, had pointed to FAA licensing support for return-to-launch-site and catch operations.
claims.supporting_quote: Gwynne Shotwell had pre-flight comments on FAA licensing support for RTLS/catch.

claims.claim: Post-flight reporting did not describe a dramatic SPCX stock swing tied directly to the Flight 15 outcome.
claims.episode_span: On SPCX, post-flight reporting in the research did not describe a dramatic move tied directly to the Flight 15 outcome.
claims.supporting_quote: Post-flight specifics limited in results; stock traded in ~$139 range around the event with no dramatic reported swing tied directly to Flight 15 outcome.
